automaticChecks.detail: Generate a 12-frame player dancing spritesheet on a 128x128 calibration tile at exactly 12 fps. Keep one player design with nominal 160px standing height, the same anatomy scale and floor-center foot/root anchor in every frame. Remove the calibration floor, retain complete limbs, and deliver a playable loop. Deliver each sprite in a 192x320px frame with local projected ground anchor (96,248). Arrange the isolated source panels in 4 columns and 3 rows, in the stated frame order. Save original generated images, exact prompts, all references, processed sprites, result.json, and review previews in /Users/yiouchen/.codex/worktrees/1834/tile-foundry/assets/evals/2026-10-17-3d-creative-reskin-all/dancing-player.

visualChecks.detail: Independent LLM identity, grading policy and hashes of originals, sprites, registration and result metadata
All twelve poses retain a coherent elevated front view, with top-facing hair/shoulders and consistent light.
All limbs and hair remain complete inside the frames; no subject is clipped or replaced by the 3D control.
The new boot/heel region falls below the original support center at the same root. The reference/candidate pairs show leg-length/support displacement rather than merely added toe length.
The same brown-haired adventurer, blue tunic, belt and brown boots persists; facial expression and arm gestures change consistently.
Twelve complete upper-body dance gestures with distinct elbow/fist and head positions are readable, with no missing/fused limbs.
Compared at unchanged roots, the refined legs and boots lengthen the standing body. This is a nominal anatomy-scale change, not a raised-arm silhouette or a crouch.
Soles/support move upward between sheet rows and through the final-to-first transition. The native frame00/frame11 pair shows an unintended vertical foot shift while metadata roots remain fixed.
Clean light/dark edges retain complete shoes, with no colored floor residue or holes in the usable sprites.
Actual 12fps playback visits all12 frames and wraps, but the final pose returns to frame1 with an unintended support/vertical-placement step. Playback validity does not make that transition seamless.
Fixed-panel extraction preserves the original reskin, including the expanded legs and row-dependent placement. No per-frame fitting, floor key or renderer-alpha stencil is used.
